question: A keyboard is hardware because you can touch it! 🎹
justification: Hardware is anything you can touch on a computer. A keyboard is something you can touch, so it is hardware!

question: What is a computer? 💻
choices: A machine that helps us do things
justification: A computer is a smart machine that helps us do many things like learning, playing games, and talking to friends!

question: A video game on your computer is software! 🎮
justification: Software is programs that run inside the computer. Games are programs, so they are software! You can't touch software.

question: You want to make a game window fill the whole screen! 🖥️ Which button should you click?
justification: The maximize button looks like a square and makes the window fill the whole screen. It's at the top-right corner!

question: When you click minimize, the window goes to the _____ of the screen. 📍
justification: Minimize hides the window at the bottom of the screen in the taskbar. It's still there, just hiding!

question: Which one is hardware? 🤔
justification: The mouse is hardware because you can touch it! Games, apps, and websites are all software that runs inside the computer.

question: Disk C: is where the computer keeps its important files! 💾
justification: Disk C: is like a big storage box where the computer keeps its programs and important files!

question: You finished playing a game and want to close it. What do you click? 🎮
justification: The X button at the top-right corner closes the app completely. Always click X when you're done!

question: You have a drawing app AND a game open. How can you quickly switch between them? ✨
choices: Click on the taskbar or use Alt+Tab
justification: You can click on the app in the taskbar at the bottom, or press Alt+Tab to switch between open windows quickly!

question: Computers help us learn, play games, and talk to friends! 🌟
justification: Computers are very useful! They help us learn new things, play fun games, and communicate with people we love.

question: To open an app on the desktop, you _____ on its icon. 🖱️
justification: Double-click means clicking the mouse button twice very quickly. This is how we open apps and files!

question: Your friend says 'A game app is hardware!' Is your friend right? 🤔
choices: Yes, because games are on the computer
No, a game app is software because you cannot touch it
justification: Your friend is wrong! Hardware is things you can touch (like the keyboard). Software is programs you cannot touch (like games and apps).

question: To move a window, you click and drag the _____ at the top. 🪟
justification: The title bar is the bar at the very top of a window. Click and drag it to move the window anywhere you want!

question: What is a folder like? 📁
choices: A toy box that holds toys
justification: A folder is like a toy box! It holds many things (files) inside it, just like a toy box holds many toys.

question: Organizing files helps us find things faster! 🔍
justification: When we organize files in folders, we can find them easily. It's like keeping your toys in the right places!

question: Which is a GOOD name for a file with your drawings? 🎨
justification: Good file names tell you what's inside! 'My Drawings' is clear and easy to understand. The other names are confusing.

question: The letters after the dot in a file name (like .txt) are called the file _____. 📄
justification: The file extension (like .txt, .png, .jpg) tells the computer what type of file it is!

question: How do you create a new folder on the desktop? 📁✨
choices: Right-click, then choose New, then Folder
justification: To create a new folder, right-click on the desktop, click 'New', then click 'Folder'. Then you can name it!

question: A file path is like a _____. It tells us where a file lives! 🏠
justification: A file path (like C:\Users\Student\Pictures) is like a home address. It tells exactly where to find the file!

question: A file ending in .txt is a text file! 📝
justification: Yes! The .txt extension means it's a text file. Like notes you write in Notepad!

question: A _____ holds files and can also hold other _____ inside it! 📁📁
justification: A folder can hold files AND other folders inside it! It's like a box that can have smaller boxes inside.

question: Which file extension means it's a PICTURE? 🖼️
justification: The .png extension (and .jpg) are for picture files! .txt is for text, .docx is for Word documents, and .mp3 is for music.

question: C:\Users\Ali\Documents\homework.txt tells us the homework file is in the Documents folder! 📂
justification: The path shows us the file's location step by step: Disk C → Users → Ali → Documents → homework.txt

question: Folders can hold many files inside them! 📁🎉
justification: Yes! A folder is like a container or box that can hold many files. This helps us stay organized!

question: Sara has 4 files. Which name is BAD and will make her confused later? 😵
justification: 'New folder (3)' is a bad name because it doesn't tell you what's inside! Good names describe what the file or folder contains.

question: What is Notepad on the computer? 📝
choices: A simple app for writing text
justification: Notepad is a simple app that lets you write text. It's like a blank piece of paper on your computer!

question: The keyboard is used for typing letters and numbers! 🎹
justification: Yes! The keyboard has keys with letters, numbers, and symbols that we press to type on the computer.

question: What does Ctrl+C do? ✨
justification: Ctrl+C is the shortcut for COPY! It makes a copy of what you selected, like making a twin of your text or picture.

question: You copied a picture of a cat 🐱. Now you want to put it somewhere else. Which shortcut do you use?
justification: Ctrl+V is PASTE! After you copy something with Ctrl+C, you use Ctrl+V to put it in a new place.

question: To save your work so you don't lose it, press _____! 💾
justification: Ctrl+S is the shortcut for SAVE! Always save your work so you can find it later. S is for Save!

question: Ctrl+X is called CUT because it moves something to a new place (not copy)! ✂️
justification: CUT (Ctrl+X) removes the item from its original place and lets you paste it somewhere else. COPY makes a twin, but CUT moves it!

question: What is the difference between COPY (Ctrl+C) and CUT (Ctrl+X)? 🤔
choices: Copy makes a twin, Cut moves the original
justification: COPY keeps the original and makes a copy. CUT removes the original and moves it to a new location when you paste!

question: Why do we write notes on a computer? 📝✨
justification: We write notes to remember things! Just like writing in a notebook, but on the computer so we can save and find them easily.

question: To switch between English and Arabic on the keyboard, press _____! 🌍
justification: Alt+Shift is the magic shortcut that switches your keyboard language between English and Arabic (or other languages)!

question: The keyboard is important for typing AND for using shortcuts! ⌨️
justification: Yes! We use the keyboard to type words AND to use special shortcuts like Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V that make things faster!

question: Why do we save files as PDF? 📄
choices: It looks the same on every computer
justification: PDF files keep the same look everywhere! Whether you open it on a computer, tablet, or phone, it looks exactly the same.

question: You typed 'Helllo' by mistake and want to remove the extra 'l'. What should you do? ❌
choices: Press the Delete or Backspace key
justification: The Delete or Backspace key removes letters or characters. Backspace deletes to the left, Delete removes to the right!

question: If you don't save your work (Ctrl+S), you might lose everything if the computer turns off! 😱
justification: Always save your work! If the computer turns off or the app closes, unsaved work disappears forever. Press Ctrl+S often!

question: To move text from one place to another, first _____ it, then _____ it in the new place!
justification: To MOVE something: First CUT it (Ctrl+X) to remove it, then PASTE it (Ctrl+V) in the new location!

question: What is a screenshot? 📸
choices: A picture of what's on your screen
justification: A screenshot is like taking a photo of your computer screen! It captures exactly what you see at that moment.

question: Screenshots are useful for saving something you want to remember! 🌟
justification: Yes! Screenshots help you save important things you see on screen, like game achievements, messages, or information!

question: Which button can take a screenshot of your whole screen? 📷
justification: The Print Screen (PrtSc) button takes a picture of your entire screen! You can find it at the top of your keyboard.

question: You got a high score in a game! 🎮🏆 Why might you take a screenshot?
choices: To save and show your achievement
justification: Screenshots let you save special moments like high scores! You can show friends or keep it as a memory of your achievement.

question: Screenshots are usually saved in the _____ folder on your computer. 📁
justification: Screenshots are pictures, so they go to the Pictures folder! Look in Pictures > Screenshots to find them.

question: You can send a screenshot to a friend or teacher to show them what you see! 👫
justification: Yes! Screenshots are great for sharing. You can send them to show someone what you're seeing on your screen!

question: Your computer shows a strange error message! 🆘 How can a screenshot help?
choices: Show the error to an adult who can help fix it
justification: Taking a screenshot of an error helps! You can show it to a parent or teacher so they know exactly what the problem looks like.

question: What is the Snipping Tool used for? ✂️📸
choices: Taking screenshots of part of the screen
justification: The Snipping Tool lets you choose exactly which part of the screen to capture, instead of the whole screen!

question: Pressing Windows + Print Screen takes a screenshot AND _____ it automatically! 💾📸
justification: Windows + Print Screen is super helpful! It takes the screenshot AND saves it to your Pictures folder automatically.

question: A screenshot captures exactly what you see on your screen at that moment! 👀
justification: A screenshot is like a camera for your screen! It captures everything showing at that exact moment.

question: You pressed Print Screen. Now you want to put the screenshot in a document. What do you press? 📋
justification: When you press Print Screen, the image is copied to the clipboard. Press Ctrl+V to paste it into a document!

question: What is a browser? 🌐
choices: A program that lets us visit websites
justification: A browser is like a magic door to the internet! It's a program that lets us visit websites and watch videos online.

question: Which one is a browser? 💻
justification: Chrome is a browser made by Google! Other browsers include Firefox, Safari, and Edge. Notepad, Calculator, and Paint are different apps.

question: We use a browser to watch YouTube videos and learn new things! 📺🌟
justification: Yes! Browsers help us visit websites like YouTube to watch videos, play games, and learn amazing things!

question: What is a tab in a browser? 📑
choices: A way to have many websites open at once
justification: Tabs are like bookmarks in a book! Each tab can show a different website, so you can have many pages open at once.

question: To open a new tab in the browser, you can press _____! 📑✨
justification: Ctrl+T opens a new Tab! The T stands for Tab. You can also click the + button next to your tabs.

question: The words on a website are too small! 🔍 How can you make them BIGGER?
justification: Ctrl + Plus (+) zooms in and makes things bigger! Ctrl + Minus (-) makes things smaller. Very helpful!

question: Downloading means getting a file from the internet to your computer! ⬇️
justification: Yes! When you download something, you're bringing a copy of it from the internet to save on your computer.

question: You downloaded a picture from the internet. Where can you find it? 📁🖼️
justification: Downloaded files go to the Downloads folder! That's where your computer saves everything you get from the internet.

question: What is browser history? 📜
choices: A list of websites you visited before
justification: Browser history is like a diary of websites! It remembers all the websites you visited, so you can find them again.

question: Oh no! You accidentally closed a tab! 😱 Press _____ to bring it back!
justification: Ctrl+Shift+T is the magic rescue shortcut! It brings back the last tab you closed. T for Tab!

question: How do you search for something in a browser? 🔍
choices: Type what you want to find and press Enter
justification: To search, type your question or what you want to find in the address bar, then press Enter! The browser will show you results.

question: Pop-up ads are messages that appear suddenly on websites, often trying to sell something! 🪟
justification: Pop-ups are surprise windows that appear suddenly. Many of them are ads trying to get you to click or buy something.

question: Why can online ads be dangerous? ⚠️
choices: They might have viruses or trick you into clicking bad things
justification: Some ads can be dangerous! They might contain viruses, trick you into clicking bad links, or ask for your personal information.

question: A colorful ad pops up saying 'You won a prize! Click here!' 🎁 What should you do?
choices: Click it quickly to get the prize
Don't click it and ask an adult
Tell all your friends to click too
justification: Never click on surprise prize ads! They are usually tricks. Always ask a parent or adult before clicking on ads.

question: Adblock is a tool that helps stop annoying ads from showing! 🛡️
justification: Adblock is a helpful tool that blocks most ads, making browsing safer and less annoying. Parents can install it!

question: What is binary? 🤖
choices: A special language with only 0 and 1
justification: Binary is the secret language of computers! It only uses two numbers: 0 and 1. That's how computers understand everything!

question: Binary only has two numbers: 0 and 1! 🔢
justification: Yes! Binary is super simple - just 0 and 1. But computers use these two numbers to do amazing things!

question: Why do computers use binary (0 and 1)? 💡
choices: Because electricity is either ON or OFF
justification: Computers run on electricity, which is either ON (1) or OFF (0). Binary matches this perfectly! Like a light switch.

question: In binary, 1 means _____ and 0 means _____. 💡
justification: In binary: 1 = ON/YES/TRUE and 0 = OFF/NO/FALSE. Just like a light switch - on or off!

question: Computers understand English and Arabic just like we do! 🗣️
justification: Computers only understand binary (0 and 1)! Special programs help translate our words into binary so computers can understand.

question: What is a problem? 🤔
choices: Something that needs to be fixed or done
justification: A problem is something that needs a solution - like a question that needs an answer or a goal we want to reach!

question: What is the FIRST step to solve a problem? 🧩
justification: Before solving anything, you must understand the problem first! Ask yourself: What is wrong? What do I need to do?

question: To solve a problem: 1) Understand it, 2) Think of solutions, 3) Try the best one, 4) _____ if it worked! ✅
justification: After trying a solution, always CHECK if it worked! If not, try again with a different idea. That's smart problem solving!

question: Making a sandwich is like solving a problem! What's the correct ORDER? 🥪
choices: Close sandwich → Eat → Get bread → Add cheese
Get bread → Add cheese → Close sandwich → Eat
Eat → Get bread → Add cheese → Close sandwich
Add cheese → Eat → Close sandwich → Get bread
justification: Steps must be in the right order! First get bread, then add cheese, close the sandwich, and finally eat it. Order matters!

question: Learning to solve problems helps us in school and in everyday life! 🌟🧠
justification: Problem solving is a super skill! It helps with homework, finding lost toys, making decisions, and even programming computers!

question: What is programming? 💻✨
justification: Programming is telling the computer what to do! We give it instructions, and it follows them to create games, apps, and websites.

question: Programming is used to create the games and apps we love! 🎮📱
justification: Yes! All games, apps, and websites are made by programmers who write instructions for computers to follow.

question: What is an algorithm? 📝
choices: A set of steps to solve a problem
justification: An algorithm is like a recipe! It's a set of steps you follow in order to solve a problem or complete a task.

question: Which of these is an example of an algorithm? 🤔
choices: Steps to brush your teeth in order
justification: An algorithm is steps in order! Brushing teeth: 1) Get toothbrush, 2) Add toothpaste, 3) Brush teeth, 4) Rinse mouth.

question: An algorithm is like a _____ for cooking - steps you follow in order! 👨‍🍳
justification: An algorithm is like a recipe! Both tell you what to do step by step in the correct order to get the result you want.

question: What is pseudocode? 📋
choices: Writing instructions in simple words to plan a program
justification: Pseudocode is writing your plan in simple words before writing real code. It helps you think about what the program will do!

question: Pseudocode is NOT real computer code - it's just a plan written in simple words! 📝
justification: Correct! Pseudocode is like planning in plain language. It helps programmers think before they write the real code.

question: Which one is an example of pseudocode? 🌧️☂️
choices: IF it is raining THEN take umbrella
justification: 'IF it is raining THEN take umbrella' is pseudocode! It's a simple plan written in words that describes what to do.

question: What is a bug in programming? 🐛
choices: A mistake that makes the program not work correctly
justification: A bug is a mistake in the program that makes it do something wrong! The name comes from a real bug found in an old computer long ago.

question: Finding and fixing bugs in a program is called _____! 🔍🐛
justification: Debugging means finding bugs (mistakes) and fixing them! It's like being a detective looking for clues to solve a mystery.

question: Why is debugging an important skill for programmers? 🦸
choices: All programs have bugs that need to be fixed
justification: Almost all programs have bugs! Good programmers know how to find and fix them. Debugging makes programs work correctly.

question: The word 'bug' in programming came from a real insect found inside an old computer! 🐛💻
justification: True! Long ago, a real moth was found stuck in an old computer causing problems. That's why we call programming mistakes 'bugs'!

question: What is cyber security? 🛡️
justification: Cyber security means staying safe on the internet! It's like locking your door at home, but for your computer and information.

question: Which of these is personal information that should stay PRIVATE? 🔒
justification: Your home address is personal information! Never share it with strangers online. Favorite colors and movies are safe to share.

question: Your full name, phone number, and school name are personal information! 📋🔐
justification: Yes! Your name, phone number, address, school name, and birthday are all personal information. Keep them private online!

question: What is a password? 🔑
choices: A secret word that opens your accounts
justification: A password is like a secret key! It keeps your accounts safe and only lets you in when you type the right word.

question: Which password is the STRONGEST? 💪🔐
justification: Sun7!Moon3@Star is strong because it mixes letters, numbers, and symbols! Simple words like 'password' or '123456' are easy to guess.

question: You should NEVER share your password with anyone except your _____! 🤫
justification: Only share passwords with your parents or guardians! They help keep you safe. Never share with friends, strangers, or online people.

question: Using your name or '123456' as a password is a BAD idea! ❌
justification: Yes, these are bad passwords! They're too easy to guess. Good passwords mix letters, numbers, and symbols.

question: A stranger online says they're a kid and wants to be your friend. What should you do? 🚨
choices: Share your address so they can visit
Tell a parent or adult immediately
justification: Always tell a parent or adult! Online strangers might not be who they say they are. Never share personal information with them.

question: It's okay to meet someone from the internet in real life without telling your parents! 🚫
justification: NEVER meet someone from the internet without your parents! Online strangers can be dangerous. Always tell a trusted adult.

question: A website says 'Click here for FREE games!' 🎮 What should you do?
choices: Click immediately to get free games
Share the link with all your friends
justification: Always ask a parent before clicking unknown links or downloading! Some 'free' offers can be tricks with viruses.

question: If something scary or bad happens online, the FIRST thing you should do is tell a _____! 🆘
justification: Always tell a parent or teacher if something bad happens online! They can help keep you safe. Don't respond to scary messages.

question: What is the FIRST rule of internet safety? 🥇🛡️
justification: Rule 1: Keep personal info private! Never share your name, address, school, phone number, or password with strangers online.

question: Rule 3 of internet safety: _____ before you click! 🧠👆
justification: Think before you click! Ask yourself: Is this safe? Do I know this website? Should I ask an adult first?
